description: An Axum-based Rust web framework with Lean 4-verifiable application kernels that run on servers, bare-metal embedded devices, and GPUs, plus integrated security testing.

written.description: Gives an agent a browser that controls its own network traffic, so the model can capture, edit, replay and compare the requests a web app sends without a proxy in between. Each session runs under a network policy and records every fetch it allowed or refused.

alive.last_commit_message:
update the video (#822)

* Film: flash the thermostat to a microcontroller in the closing shot

The engineer now deploys the board app and then flashes
examples/embedded/thermostat to a XIAO RP2040 on the desk; the camera
settles on its LED turning green. The caption becomes "Proven in Lean 4.
Shipped as Rust, to servers and microcontrollers." The engineer shot runs
36-42 s and the end card 42-48 s. The demo page links the embedded
example and scopes the claim to its interlock theorem and h1 parser.

* Film: open on the web apps around us, so the embedded ending pays off

The opening is now an 8 s crane move through the engineer's room. A robot
vacuum crosses the floor, then the camera passes a small server rack and a
smart speaker on the desk and settles on the engineer at the laptop. Each
device shows a floating tag with an HTTP route (GET /map, GET /api/posts,
POST /volume, localhost:8080). The captions are "Web apps run everywhere,
from servers to the devices around you." and, as the tags turn red,
"Every one of them is a target." The devices are built from primitives in
scene.py and illustrate where web apps run; the page and README say the
film does not claim they run h5i.

Everything after the opening moves 3 s later (the film is 51 s, PT51S).
The hard-coded times in scene.py, screens.py, audio.py and compose.py move
with it, and the poster is the same proof frame at 16 s. The soundtrack
adds a vacuum motor, a ping per tag and a low hit when the tags turn red.

* Film: close on the opening's devices, now proven, instead of flashing a board

The closing shot pulls back from the deploy to the whole room. The vacuum,
speaker, rack and laptop tags return red, then a green ring spreads from
the laptop and each tag turns green with a check mark. Captions are now
"Proven in Lean 4. Shipped as Rust." and "From servers to robots, wherever
web apps run." The XIAO flashing beat is gone (its LED turning green is a
background detail), as is "microcontrollers" from captions and screens.
index.html and README.md say "embedded and edge devices" and state that
the devices illustrate where h5i is meant to be used, not that they run it.

Code and docs only: media/demo/h5i-demo.mp4 and docs/demo/assets/poster.jpg
are unchanged and still show the previous ending. They will be regenerated
by the next full render.

* Film: realism pass for the rooms and the hoodies

CC0 Poly Haven textures and props (pinned, checksummed, downloaded into
out/ by film/assets.py), a night city with depth behind the window,
practical lamp and city light, sculpted hoodie folds, cuffs, hem band,
pocket and drawstrings, motion blur, and lens effects in compose.py.

* Film: no windows on the city's roofs; a shorter shutter keeps the tags legible

* Film docs: credit the Poly Haven assets and describe the realism pass

* Film: a larger EEVEE shadow pool, so the opening's crane move keeps its shadows

* Film: publish the realism render (new ending included)

Full render with the realism pass and the merged ending: 51 s, 1080p24,
18.3 MB. The network shot (frames 577-816) is reused from the previous
render; its scene did not change.

* Film: hold the closing caption a second longer

The closing shot runs 39-47 s and the end card 47-52 s, so "From servers
to robots, wherever web apps run." stays on screen about a second longer
over the room. The film is now 52 s; the pages and READMEs say so, and the
front page's film card no longer says 0:48.
